dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Sir Yun's opera performances are truly extraordinary. Well worth the trip to come see it today.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey there, Zhongli. You're here too, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed. A pleasure to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: With little to do at the Funeral Parlor these past few days, I asked the Director for some time off, during which I've been traveling around a bit, and visiting some old friends in passing.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I just happened to pass by as Sir Yun was performing, and I could not help but sit down and watch the entire performance.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: She exercises wondrous command of this folk art. So absorbed was I in the performance that I forgot to drink even a single cup of the tea I had ordered.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: To drink tea of such refinement cold, when much of its flavor has been lost... A shame indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you have friends around here as well?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: An ancient adage says, "As lush mountains may be found everywhere, so too may friends be met."

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: But my dear associates are busy at the moment, and I don't wish to disturb them.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Checking on them from afar and sending them letters at suitable times will suffice.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: *sigh* Truly, I have done this fine pot of tea a disservice...
